sentences.en: He would stand up for himself.

sentences.en: Last week on the show, we examined the science of conversation.
sentences.zh: 上周的节目中，我们探讨了对话的科学。

sentences.en: We looked at why an ordinary chat is far from ordinary.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了为什么一场普通的聊天其实一点也不普通。

sentences.en: These interactions involve hundreds of micro-decisions
sentences.zh: 这些互动涉及数百个微小的决策，

sentences.en: and a delicate dance of coordination.

sentences.en: It's called We Need to Talk.

sentences.en: Today, we look at the conversations we all dread.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来看看我们都害怕的那些对话。

sentences.en: Telling someone they treated us poorly.

sentences.en: Taking away an elderly relative's car keys.

sentences.en: Alison Woodbrooks is a behavioral scientist at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·伍德布鲁克斯是哈佛商学院的行为科学家。

sentences.en: She studies the art and science of conversations
sentences.zh: 她研究对话的艺术与科学，

sentences.en: and how we can get better at having difficult conversations.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何才能更好地进行困难的对话。

sentences.en: Alison Woodbrooks, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·伍德布鲁克斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Alison, one way we mishandle difficult conversations
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，我们处理困难对话不当的一种方式，

sentences.en: is that we avoid having them all together.
sentences.zh: 就是完全避免进行这些对话。

sentences.en: How common is such evasion?
sentences.zh: 这种回避现象有多普遍？

sentences.en: Avoidance is so common.
sentences.zh: 回避非常普遍。

sentences.en: And it's common in my life, too.
sentences.zh: 在我的生活中也很普遍。

sentences.en: I'm an avoider.
sentences.zh: 我就是一个回避者。

sentences.en: And so I deeply understand why so many people avoid having hard conversations.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常理解为什么那么多人回避进行艰难的对话。

sentences.en: They avoid people that they know will be hard to interact with,
sentences.zh: 他们回避那些他们知道很难相处的人，

sentences.en: and they avoid topics that feel at least ahead of time like they're going to be very difficult
sentences.zh: 他们回避那些至少在预想中会非常困难的话题，

sentences.en: for any number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因有很多。

sentences.en: You know, I remember many years ago as a small child,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得很多年前还是个小孩子的时候，

sentences.en: my grandfather, you know, had rented out an apartment to someone,
sentences.zh: 我祖父把一套公寓租给了别人，

sentences.en: and that person wasn't paying my grandfather the rent.
sentences.zh: 那个人没有付给我祖父房租。

sentences.en: And my grandfather knew he had to have, you know, a conversation with the tenant,
sentences.zh: 我祖父知道他必须和租客谈谈，

sentences.en: and basically it was going to be a difficult conversation.
sentences.zh: 基本上那会是一场困难的对话。

sentences.en: And he was a people pleaser, and he hated having difficult conversations.
sentences.zh: 他是个讨好型人格，他讨厌进行困难的对话。

sentences.en: So whenever he saw the tenant, you know, come up the other side of the road,
sentences.zh: 所以每当他看到租客从马路对面走过来时，

sentences.en: you know, he would run and hide in the bushes
sentences.zh: 他就会跑去灌木丛里躲起来，

sentences.en: because he didn't want to have, you know, the difficult conversation with the tenant.
sentences.zh: 因为他不想和租客进行那场困难的对话。

sentences.en: And, of course, as a small child, you look at that,
sentences.zh: 当然，作为一个小孩子，你看着那一幕，

sentences.en: and you realize, oh, these are difficult conversations.
sentences.zh: 你会意识到，噢，这些就是困难的对话。

sentences.en: One way to handle them is to basically not have them at all.
sentences.zh: 处理它们的一种方式基本上就是完全不进行对话。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's not always the wrong instinct,
sentences.zh: 这并不总是错误的本能，

sentences.en: but you do have to sort of think about who is it leading us to avoid and why.
sentences.zh: 但你确实需要思考一下，这导致我们回避了谁，为什么回避？

sentences.en: Why are we avoiding these topics?

sentences.en: And are those reasons good?

sentences.en: Are they biased?

sentences.en: Are they preventing us from having a deeper relationship?

sentences.en: I feel like I avoid certain topics often right now, maybe just today.

sentences.en: I mean, I could initiate conversations with many of my students, for example,

sentences.en: and tell them that I don't think that their performance in the course so far has been terrific

sentences.en: but their learning and also how I personally feel about them, right?
sentences.zh: 还会影响他们的学习，以及我个人对他们的看法，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it's affecting our relationship in a sort of personal way.

sentences.en: And the way I avoid that conversation is by asking my assistant to write emails to the students

sentences.en: There are so many reasons that prevent me from sort of reaching out one-on-one to them.
sentences.zh: 有太多原因阻止我一对一地去联系他们。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting, Alison.

sentences.en: to basically say, I think, or, you know, here's something to think about.

sentences.en: It goes back to this idea of our instinct says that I'm right and I'm going to prove to you that I'm right.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我需要用一种如此令人信服且强有力的方式说出来，让你无法否认我是对的。

sentences.en: And to do that, I need to say it in such a compelling and strong way that you can't possibly deny that I'm right.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记了，作为这种心态的承受方，作为倾听者，

sentences.en: We forget that it's really hard to be on the receiving end of that, to be the listener
sentences.zh: 接收这种强硬的陈述和说教式的语言是非常难受的。

sentences.en: and to be receiving such like strong statement, righteous sort of language.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于修饰你的语言，表达你不确定的观点，

sentences.en: And so this point about qualifying your language, expressing the points that you're uncertain about,
sentences.zh: 比如，我其实在想是不是这样，或者我想我相当确定是这样，或者我对这个感到好奇。

sentences.en: like, I actually was wondering if this, or I think I'm pretty sure this, or I wonder about this.

sentences.en: Those qualifications, that qualifying language goes against our instincts to be strong and resolute and decisive.
sentences.zh: 但作为承受方，这会让对方听起来合理且现实得多。

sentences.en: But being on the receiving end of it, it makes that person sound so much more reasonable and realistic.

sentences.en: And it's so much easier to engage with them.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能已经察觉到了一个主题，那就是所有这些努力都是为了能够继续交谈，

sentences.en: So you're probably detecting a theme here, which is all of this stuff goes towards the goal of being able to continue talking to each other
sentences.zh: 以一种富有成效，甚至可以说令人愉快的方式进行。

sentences.en: in a way that's productive and, dare I say, enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们顺从本能去向别人证明我们是对的，

sentences.zh: 就很难继续那场对话，而且对话会陷入一种令人不快的境地。

sentences.en: it's very hard to continue to have that conversation and it's going to spiral into a place that's not enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，前段时间我在《Hidden Brain》节目中和另一位嘉宾交谈，

sentences.en: You know, I was talking to another guest on Hidden Brain some time ago,

sentences.en: and he used to be a champion, you know, debater in high school.
sentences.zh: 当然，当你进行辩论时，你知道，你会提出你最强的论点，

sentences.en: And of course, when you're having a debate, you know, you present your strongest argument

sentences.en: and the other person presents their strongest argument, and then a judge decides whose argument is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 他指出，在很多方面，我们进行艰难对话的方式也是一样的，

sentences.en: And he was pointing out that in many ways, we conduct difficult conversations the same way,
sentences.zh: 也就是我们试图推销自己的论点，并期望对方也推销他们的论点。

sentences.en: which is we try and prosecute our argument and expect the other person is going to prosecute their argument.
sentences.zh: 然后想象有一个虚构的裁判会进来，把奖项颁给我们，

sentences.en: And then imagine that there is some kind of imaginary judge who's going to come in and give us the prize
sentences.zh: 因为我们提出了更好的论点。

sentences.en: for coming up with the better argument.
sentences.zh: 但当然，在现实生活中，没有裁判。

sentences.en: But of course, in real life, there is no judge.
sentences.zh: 没有第三方来裁决并说你的论点比对方的更好。

sentences.en: There is no third party to adjudicate and say your argument was better than the other person's argument.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你的目标是与对方沟通，并找到共同点。

sentences.en: Your goal, in fact, is to get across to the other person and to sort of find common ground with the other person.
sentences.zh: 而当你试图把对方驳得体无完肤时，这是很难做到的。

sentences.en: And that's very hard to do when you're trying to beat the other person into a pulp.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢做一个思想实验，我称之为“我的方式、你的方式、正确的方式”。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of thought experiment that I like to do that I think of as my way, your way, the right way.
sentences.zh: 对于几乎任何任务、任何话题或任何问题，我们就叫它“装洗碗机”吧。

sentences.en: For almost any task or any topic or any issue, let's just call it loading the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 我有我装洗碗机的方式。

sentences.en: I have my way of loading the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 你有你装洗碗机的方式。

sentences.en: You have your way of loading the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 但可能我们俩装洗碗机的方式都不是客观上正确或最优的方式。

sentences.en: But probably neither of our ways of loading the dishwasher is the objectively correct or optimal way of loading the dishwasher.
sentences.zh: 所以互相挑剔，争论说，嗯，我的方式是最好的。

sentences.en: And so nitpicking with each other and arguing about, well, my way is the best way.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，嗯，我的方式才是最好的。

sentences.en: And then you say, well, my way is the best way.
sentences.zh: 这一切都很愚蠢，尤其是当你们谁都不知道什么是最好的方式这种客观事实时。

sentences.en: It's all so silly, especially when neither of you knows the sort of ground truth, objective reality of what's the best way.
sentences.zh: 当你感受到的情绪是无益的负面情绪时，你说，Alison，我们应该以更积极的角度重新构建它们。

sentences.en: When the emotions we're feeling are unhelpfully negative, you say, Alison, that we should reframe them in a more positive light.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下你的意思吗？

sentences.en: Can you explain what you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你所说的“以积极的角度重新构建负面情绪”是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean by reframing a negative emotion in a positive light?
sentences.zh: 当我们感到负面情绪时，我们大多数时候都会这样，我们对如何体验这种情绪的控制力比我们想象的要大得多。

sentences.en: When we feel negative emotions, which we all do a lot of the time, we have a lot more control over how we experience that emotion than we would think.
sentences.zh: 所以我举个焦虑的例子。

sentences.en: So I'll give the example of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到焦虑时，这是一种高唤醒度的情绪。

sentences.en: When we feel anxious, it's a high arousal emotion.
sentences.zh: 它非常负面。

sentences.en: It's very negative.
sentences.zh: 我们的本能告诉我们要试着冷静下来，试着摆脱那种情绪。

sentences.en: Our instinct tells us to try and calm down, try and get rid of that emotion.
sentences.zh: 人们在感到焦虑时会竭尽全力试图冷静下来。

sentences.en: People go to great lengths to try and calm down when they're feeling anxious.
sentences.zh: 但冷静下来需要一个两步走的过程。

sentences.en: But calming down requires a sort of two-step move.
sentences.zh: 你必须降低你的生理唤醒水平。

sentences.en: You have to reduce your physiological arousal.
sentences.zh: 所以你的心跳加速、手心出汗、体内的皮质醇，这些东西真的很难控制。

sentences.en: So your racing heart, your sweaty palms, your cortisol in your body, those things are really hard to control.
sentences.zh: 你实际上对这些东西没有太多的执行控制权。

sentences.en: You actually don't have a lot of executive control over those things.
sentences.zh: 而且你试图从负面情绪转向正面情绪。

sentences.en: And you're trying to move from negative emotion to positive.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个两步走的过程，结果证明非常困难，甚至是不可能的。

sentences.en: So it's this two-step thing that turns out very hard to do, if not impossible.
sentences.zh: 重新构建的理念是，让我们专注于我们确实有更多控制权的那部分。

sentences.en: The idea of reframing is let's focus on the part of it that we do have more control over.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们对负面与正面的评估。

sentences.en: And that's our appraisal of negative versus positive.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你感到焦虑，如果我们保持在高唤醒状态，你只是对自己说，你知道吗，我很兴奋。

sentences.en: So if you're feeling anxious, what if we stay in high arousal world and you just say to yourself, you know what, I'm excited.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是这小小的转变，就能帮助你从负面效价的焦虑转向正面效价的兴奋。

sentences.en: Just that small flip helps move you from negative valence anxiety to positive valence excitement.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以把痛苦看作激情，例如，作为一种重新构建或重新评估你所经历的痛苦的方式。

sentences.en: So you can see, for example, distress as passion, for example, as a way of reframing or reappraising the distress that you're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 所以我曾与 Lizzie Bailey-Wolf 合作研究过这个问题。

sentences.en: So I have worked with Lizzie Bailey-Wolf about this.
sentences.zh: 人们经常说，我压力很大，我非常痛苦。

sentences.en: Often people say, I'm stressed, I'm so distressed.
sentences.zh: 但你可以为了自己的利益重新构建它，说，不，不，这只是一个信号，表明我在乎它，我很有激情。

sentences.en: But you can reframe that for your own benefit and saying, no, no, this is just a signal that I care about it, that I'm passionate.
sentences.zh: 而且大声说出来对周围的人也很有感染力。

sentences.en: And actually saying it out loud is really compelling to the people around you as well.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，我理解你的意思，Alison，目标与其说是改变情绪本身，不如说是改变你对情绪的解读。

sentences.en: So in some ways, what I understand you're saying, Alison, is that the goal here is not so much to change the emotion itself, but to shift your interpretation of the emotion.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 心理学家称之为“重新评估”。

sentences.en: Psychologists call this reappraisal.
sentences.zh: 你改变的是评估方式，而不是你在生理上的感受，只是你思考和解读那种感觉的方式。

sentences.en: You're shifting the appraisal, not how you're feeling physiologically, but just how you're thinking about and interpreting that feeling.
sentences.zh: 你改变的是评估方式，而不是你在生理上的感受，只是你思考和解读那种感觉的方式。

sentences.en: You have a colleague, Cynthia, who has a very effective way of reframing emotion when a discussion gets too heated.
sentences.zh: 你有一位同事叫辛西娅，当讨论变得过于激烈时，她有一种非常有效的方法来重构情绪。

sentences.en: What is her technique, Alison?
sentences.zh: 她的技巧是什么，艾莉森？

sentences.en: My colleague, Cynthia, is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我的同事辛西娅非常了不起。

sentences.en: She's an incredible teacher.
sentences.zh: 她是一位出色的老师。

sentences.en: And I love watching her teach because she constantly keeps her sort of hand on the dial, the sort of temperature knob of the mood of the classroom.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢看她教学，因为她总是能掌控课堂氛围的“刻度盘”，也就是调节课堂情绪的温度旋钮。

sentences.en: And when she feels like things are getting too down or sad or angry, she calls it out.
sentences.zh: 当她感觉到气氛变得过于低落、悲伤或愤怒时，她会指出来。

sentences.en: She says, I'm not loving the emotional vibe in here.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我不喜欢现在的这种情绪氛围。”

sentences.en: Let's hit the refresh button.
sentences.zh: “让我们按下刷新键吧。”

sentences.en: And she does, even just by labeling it and saying, let's hit the refresh button, it really helps so much.
sentences.zh: 她确实这么做了，仅仅通过给情绪贴上标签并说“让我们按下刷新键”，就非常有帮助。

sentences.en: So in other words, just like we can call attention to what's happening inside our minds and label it and say, you know, I'm feeling defensive.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就像我们可以关注内心正在发生的事情并给它贴上标签，比如“我知道，我感到防御心理很强”。

sentences.en: I'm feeling upset.
sentences.zh: “我感到心烦意乱。”

sentences.en: I'm feeling called out.
sentences.zh: “我感到被针对了。”

sentences.en: I'm feeling threatened.
sentences.zh: “我感到受到了威胁。”

sentences.en: What she is doing is saying we can call attention to what's happening in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 她所做的是告诉我们，我们可以关注对话中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Notice where we are in the chat.
sentences.zh: 注意我们在谈话中处于什么状态。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's what makes levity so powerful as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是让轻松感如此强大的原因。

sentences.en: You notice if people are getting bored or disengaged from the conversation, it's so important in those moments to realize the emotional timbre and to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到，如果人们对谈话感到厌烦或心不在焉，在那些时刻意识到情绪基调并采取行动是非常重要的。

sentences.en: Switch topics, make a joke, smile, give someone a compliment.
sentences.zh: 转换话题、开个玩笑、微笑一下，或者赞美某人。

sentences.en: Just to lift the mood is incredibly powerful.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了提升情绪，这本身就具有不可思议的力量。

sentences.en: One error we make in difficult conversations is we sometimes try to see things from the perspective of the other person, which on the surface seems like a good thing.
sentences.zh: 我们在困难对话中犯的一个错误是，有时会试图从对方的角度看问题，这表面上看起来是件好事。

sentences.en: But the problem is when we do this, we imagine how we would think and what we would do in their circumstances.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，当我们这样做时，我们想象的是自己在对方的情况下会怎么想、怎么做。

sentences.en: Talk about what happens when we do this, Alison.
sentences.zh: 谈谈当我们这样做时会发生什么，艾莉森。

sentences.en: It's such a well-meaning instinct.
sentences.zh: 这是一种出于好意的本能。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, the human mind is so egocentric.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，人类的思维是非常以自我为中心的。

sentences.en: So we try to imagine what another person would be thinking and feeling, but we use our own thoughts and feelings as a sort of proxy, as a guess.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图想象另一个人会怎么想、怎么感觉，但我们用自己的想法和感受作为一种代理，作为一种猜测。

sentences.en: This is what helps us guess how other people are thinking and feeling.
sentences.zh: 这就是帮助我们猜测他人想法和感受的方式。

sentences.en: We're relying on our own point of view.
sentences.zh: 我们依赖的是我们自己的观点。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, no two people are exactly alike.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，没有哪两个人是完全一样的。

sentences.en: Even my twin sister, Sarah, and I are not exactly alike.
sentences.zh: 即使是我和我的双胞胎姐妹莎拉，也不完全一样。

sentences.en: And most people are just incredibly different from each other.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数人彼此之间差异巨大。

sentences.en: And we underestimate how different other people are from us.
sentences.zh: 我们低估了其他人与我们之间的差异程度。

sentences.en: So very famously, psychologists have found that people are just really, it's very challenging to take another person's perspective.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有一个非常著名的发现，即人们真的很难站在他人的角度看问题。

sentences.en: The most direct way to take another person's perspective isn't to guess, but to ask them for it.
sentences.zh: 站在他人角度看问题最直接的方法不是猜测，而是直接询问他们。

sentences.en: To ask questions and actually hear from their own mouth what's going on in their mind.
sentences.zh: 通过提问，亲耳听听他们内心真实的想法。

sentences.en: When we come back, why seemingly innocuous comments can deeply hurt another person and a magic key to disarming someone who is very angry with you.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨为什么看似无害的评论会深深伤害他人，以及化解对方强烈愤怒的魔法钥匙。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》(Hidden Brain)。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Have you ever noticed that when you're having a difficult conversation, or even a conversation that wasn't supposed to be difficult,
sentences.zh: 你有没有注意到，当你进行一场困难的对话，甚至是本不该困难的对话时，

sentences.en: something you say can set off another person and send the conversation hey, you are?
sentences.zh: 你说的话可能会触怒对方，让谈话变得……嘿，你在干什么？

sentences.en: You are not trying to give offense, but the other person is deeply offended.
sentences.zh: 你并不是想冒犯对方，但对方却感到深受冒犯。

sentences.en: At Harvard Business School, Alison Woodbrook says she teaches her students an exercise to avoid such landmines.
sentences.zh: 哈佛商学院的艾莉森·伍德布鲁克说，她教学生一种练习来避免这种地雷。

sentences.en: My students find it helpful to use a model to think about why these difficult moments pop up in conversations,
sentences.zh: 我的学生发现使用一个模型来思考为什么这些困难时刻会在对话中出现是很有帮助的，

sentences.en: sometimes unexpectedly, often unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 有时是出乎意料的，通常都是出乎意料的。

sentences.en: And we use a model that we call the layers of the earth.
sentences.zh: 我们使用一个我们称之为“地球分层”的模型。

sentences.en: Above the surface of the earth, this is the content of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 在地球表面之上，这是对话的内容。

sentences.en: So the words that we're saying to each other, the sound, the way we sound to each other,
sentences.zh: 也就是我们对彼此说的话、声音、我们听起来的感觉，

sentences.en: our nonverbal cues, all the things that are observable above the surface.
sentences.zh: 我们的非语言暗示，所有在表面上可以观察到的东西。

sentences.en: Right at the surface of the earth are our emotions, and sometimes parts of our emotions are observable.
sentences.zh: 就在地表处是我们的情绪，有时部分情绪是可以观察到的。

sentences.en: You can tell when I'm getting angry or anxious or upset, and sometimes they're hidden beneath the surface of the earth.
sentences.zh: 你能看出我什么时候变得愤怒、焦虑或心烦，有时它们隐藏在地球表面之下。

sentences.en: Right below that layer are our motives or our goals.
sentences.zh: 在那一层之下是我们的动机或目标。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe sometimes I want to seek your advice, but you don't want to give it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许有时我想寻求你的建议，但你不想给。

sentences.en: Or I want to persuade you, but you are not ready to be persuaded.
sentences.zh: 或者我想说服你，但你还没准备好被说服。

sentences.en: When we have incongruous motives, it's another way that difficult moments can erupt.
sentences.zh: 当我们有不一致的动机时，这是困难时刻爆发的另一种方式。

sentences.en: And then at the very core of the earth, of course, are our differences in our identities.
sentences.zh: 当然，在地球的最核心，是我们身份认知的差异。

sentences.en: And any time conversation shoots down to the hot magma of our identity,
sentences.zh: 每当谈话深入到我们身份认知的炽热岩浆时，

sentences.en: things are going to feel really hot and heated and difficult.
sentences.zh: 事情就会变得非常火热、激烈和困难。

sentences.en: And even sort of easy conversations have a way of shooting down to that hot magma core of our identities in sort of unexpected ways.
sentences.zh: 即使是看似轻松的谈话，也可能以某种意想不到的方式深入到我们身份认知的岩浆核心。

sentences.en: And my students talk about this a lot.
sentences.zh: 我的学生经常谈论这个。

sentences.en: But, like, you know, you can even an innocuous question like, oh, where did you get your glasses?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，甚至是一个无害的问题，比如“哦，你的眼镜是在哪买的？”

sentences.en: Or, hey, I love your haircut,
sentences.zh: 或者“嘿，我很喜欢你的发型”，

sentences.en: can feel sort of deeply threatening to people if they're imagining that this question is going to lead to something very sensitive about their identity
sentences.zh: 如果人们认为这个问题会引出关于他们身份认知的非常敏感的话题，

sentences.en: or where they're from or their race or their gender or their, you know, sexual orientation.
sentences.zh: 或者关于他们来自哪里、种族、性别，或者你知道，性取向的问题，这可能会让人感到深深的威胁。

sentences.en: And so what we talk about in my class is becoming a little bit more aware of differences at every layer of the earth.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在课堂上讨论的是，要对地球每一层的差异变得更加敏感。

sentences.en: So at the surface where our words, are we literally using the same, the right words?
sentences.zh: 在表面层，关于我们的言语，我们是否真的使用了相同、正确的词汇？

sentences.en: Are we understanding each other and what we mean when we're using certain words?
sentences.zh: 我们是否理解彼此在使用某些词汇时的含义？

sentences.en: And often moments of difficulty come from like, oh, we're just misunderstanding each other.
sentences.zh: 通常困难时刻源于，哦，我们只是误解了对方。

sentences.en: We're using the same word to mean different things or we're not talking about the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我们用同一个词表达不同的意思，或者我们谈论的根本不是同一件事。

sentences.en: Often these differences in our emotions cause probleMs.
sentences.zh: 通常这些情绪上的差异会导致问题。

sentences.en: I want to go have fun.
sentences.zh: 我想去玩得开心。

sentences.en: You actually want to have a deep conversation.
sentences.zh: 而你实际上想进行一次深入的交谈。

sentences.en: We have different motives.
sentences.zh: 我们有不同的动机。

sentences.en: And then, of course, differences in our identities.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有我们身份认知的差异。

sentences.en: And I think most of the most difficult moments in conversation come from the moments when you poke an invisible barb into somebody's identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为对话中最困难的时刻，大多源于你无意中触碰了某人身份认知中隐形的倒刺。

sentences.en: And sometimes you realize when it's happened and sometimes you don't.
sentences.zh: 有时你意识到发生了什么，有时则没有。

sentences.en: It goes back to the story of this LGBTQ student who came and talked to me about making an insensitive comment, a heteronormative comment in class.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起那个LGBTQ学生的故事，他来找我谈论我在课堂上发表的不敏感言论，一种异性恋霸权的言论。

sentences.en: I poked an invisible barb into an important part of who he is, and he didn't feel seen and acknowledged and valued and worthy of care.
sentences.zh: 我触碰了他身份中重要部分的一根隐形倒刺，他感到自己没有被看见、被认可、被重视，也没有得到应有的关怀。

sentences.en: And so any time that we make our conversation partner feel like we don't understand them, we don't see them, and we are not making them feel worthy of care,
sentences.zh: 所以，任何时候如果我们让谈话对象觉得我们不理解他们、看不见他们，并且没有让他们感到值得被关怀，

sentences.en: it's going to cause probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这都会导致问题。

sentences.en: When you were a college student, Allison, you and your fellow students found yourselves in opposition to an administrator.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，当你还是大学生时，你和同学们发现自己与一位行政人员处于对立面。

sentences.en: The students saw this administrator as an enforcer, and they thought that she was heavy-handed.
sentences.zh: 学生们把这位行政人员视为执行者，认为她手段强硬。

sentences.en: They often clashed with her.
sentences.zh: 他们经常与她发生冲突。

sentences.en: You decided to try another approach.
sentences.zh: 你决定尝试另一种方法。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: So I was a member of a club, a social club, when I was an undergrad,
sentences.zh: 我读本科时是一个社交俱乐部的成员，

sentences.en: and there was a woman there whose full-time job it was to take care of this beautiful property and to keep all of the students who hung out there and ate their meals there,
sentences.zh: 那里有一位女士，她的全职工作是打理这处美丽的房产，并确保所有在那里消磨时间、用餐的学生，

sentences.en: to keep them safe.
sentences.zh: 确保他们的安全。

sentences.en: And historically, the student members of the club had this really confrontational sort of oppositional relationship with this house manager.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，俱乐部的学生成员与这位宿舍管理员之间一直存在这种非常对抗性的对立关系。

sentences.en: And I remember watching this oppositional dynamic unfold, and it really made me feel not only uncomfortable,
sentences.zh: 我记得看着这种对立的动态发展，这不仅让我感到不舒服，

sentences.en: but also I started to feel like this isn't serving the students well either, because it puts her in this enforcer position, in this oppositional position.
sentences.zh: 而且我开始觉得这对学生也没有好处，因为它把她置于执行者的位置，置于这种对立的位置。

sentences.en: She's not going to give us the things that we want.
sentences.zh: 她不会给我们想要的东西。

sentences.en: And so when I became the sort of vice president of this club, I thought, I'm going to try and convince my fellow students, the fellow leaders of the club, and this woman,
sentences.zh: 所以当我成为俱乐部的副主席时，我想，我要试着说服我的同学、俱乐部的其他领导者，以及这位女士，

sentences.en: let's reposition ourselves as allies.
sentences.zh: 让我们把自己重新定位为盟友。

sentences.en: Like, why don't we try and work together?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不试着一起合作呢？

sentences.en: And so first I had to convince the other students that this was a good approach.
sentences.zh: 所以首先我必须说服其他学生，这是一种好的方法。

sentences.en: That was not easy, because there was a lot of animosity between the students and this house manager.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易，因为学生和这位宿舍管理员之间有很多敌意。

sentences.en: But then the really hard conversation was facing this woman myself, and I remember it very vividly.
sentences.zh: 但真正困难的谈话是亲自面对这位女士，我记得非常清楚。

sentences.en: It was at her, it was in her office, in private, sort of woman-on-woman.
sentences.zh: 那是在她的办公室里，私下里，女性对女性的交流。

sentences.en: I was the first woman who had ever been an officer in this club, and I went and met with her one-on-one.
sentences.zh: 我是这个俱乐部历史上第一位女性干部，我单独去见了她。

sentences.en: And she was so gracious and so grateful when I apologized for the behavior of all of the students historically, and how unkind they had been, and how, how,
sentences.zh: 当我为学生们历史上所有的行为，以及他们曾经是多么不友善而道歉时，她表现得非常亲切和感激，以及……

sentences.en: why this animosity had erupted between the students and this house manager.
sentences.zh: 为什么学生和这位宿舍管理员之间会爆发这种敌意。

sentences.en: And I just said, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，我非常抱歉。

sentences.en: Like, I, I, we don't want you to feel that way.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让你有那种感觉。

sentences.en: We want to work together.
sentences.zh: 我们想一起合作。

sentences.en: We want to be on the same team here.
sentences.zh: 我们想成为同一个团队。

sentences.en: And, and she just said, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 她只是说，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for saying this.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你这么说。

sentences.en: This sounds so amazing.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: And we both cried, and she was so grateful.
sentences.zh: 我们都哭了，她非常感激。

sentences.en: And it really felt like this turning point in the dynamic, which did prove out to be really great for us going forward.
sentences.zh: 这感觉确实是这种动态的转折点，事实证明这对我们未来的发展真的很好。

sentences.en: It really worked out well.
sentences.zh: 结果真的很好。

sentences.en: She gave the club so much more of what we actually wanted.
sentences.zh: 她给了俱乐部更多我们真正想要的东西。

sentences.en: And then what was really moving, it ended up being one of the most meaningful sort of conversations of my life.
sentences.zh: 最令人感动的是，这最终成了我一生中最有意义的谈话之一。

sentences.en: That was, you know, 15 years ago, and that was an inflection point for the club going forward.
sentences.zh: 那是15年前的事了，那是俱乐部未来发展的一个转折点。

sentences.en: The students then developed a new norm of being friends with this woman and being on good terms, and it continued on for the next 15 years.
sentences.zh: 学生们随后形成了一种与这位女士友好相处的新规范，这种关系持续了接下来的15年。

sentences.en: And I saw her at my 15th college reunion, and she, she looked great.
sentences.zh: 我在大学毕业15周年聚会上见到了她，她看起来气色很好。

sentences.en: She looked so healthy and happy, and she pulled me aside, and she said, I just can never thank you enough for having that conversation with me and making this change.
sentences.zh: 她看起来很健康、很幸福，她把我拉到一边说，我永远无法感谢你和我进行那次谈话并做出这种改变。

sentences.en: It changed the club for the better, and it changed my life.
sentences.zh: 它让俱乐部变得更好，也改变了我的人生。

sentences.en: And I, it meant so much to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我也意义重大。

sentences.en: Wow, that's an amazing story, Alison.
sentences.zh: 哇，这是一个了不起的故事，艾莉森。

sentences.en: And it's really testament to what happens when we handle difficult conversations well, that there is a, you know, there's a huge payoff here, a huge, you know,
sentences.zh: 这确实证明了当我们妥善处理困难对话时会发生什么，这里有巨大的回报，巨大的，你知道，

sentences.en: psychological payoff here.
sentences.zh: 心理上的回报。

sentences.en: Yeah, and don't get me wrong, it was scary to have that conversation.
sentences.zh: 是的，别误会，进行那次谈话很可怕。

sentences.en: It felt like, you know, she, she didn't like the students.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像，她不喜欢学生。

sentences.en: She was mad at us all the time.
sentences.zh: 她一直对我们很生气。

sentences.en: We were always in trouble, and there was so much historical animosity that I was trying to sort of undo and shake up.
sentences.zh: 我们总是惹麻烦，而且有太多的历史敌意，我试图去化解和改变它。

sentences.en: And it was, it was, it took a lot of chutzpahs or a lot of courage to go in there and try and sort of work through it.
sentences.zh: 这需要很大的胆量或勇气去那里尝试解决它。

sentences.en: It wasn't easy.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。

sentences.en: One of the incredibly difficult and incredibly powerful things that you did was that you apologized to her for the way that she had been treated in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 你所做的极其困难且极其有力的事情之一，就是你为她过去受到的对待向她道歉。

sentences.en: And I think for people who are, who feel like they have been wronged or people who are in opposition, there's often a sense of, you know, sort of burning injustice.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于那些觉得自己受到委屈的人，或者处于对立面的人来说，通常会有一种……某种燃烧的不公正感。

sentences.en: You know, I'm just an administrator, I'm here trying to keep the students safe, you know, all they have is ill will toward me, they treat me so badly,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只是一个行政人员，我在这里努力确保学生的安全，他们对我只有恶意，他们对我太糟糕了，

sentences.en: no one recognizes what I've done.
sentences.zh: 没有人认可我所做的一切。

sentences.en: And so you have this narrative in your head of all the ways in which the world has been unkind to you.
sentences.zh: 所以你的脑海里会有关于世界对你不友善的所有方式的叙述。

sentences.en: And of course, the world doesn't constantly come and admit that.
sentences.zh: 当然，世界不会不断地来承认这一点。

sentences.en: But when someone actually walks in the door and says, I'm sorry, it has a transformative effect on you.
sentences.zh: 但当有人真的走进门说“对不起”时，它会对你产生变革性的影响。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about the power of apologies in the course of having difficult conversations?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈在困难对话中道歉的力量吗？

sentences.en: I think as a conversation researcher, as a human being, apologies are one of the most powerful tools we have in our conversational toolkit.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一名对话研究者，作为一个人类，道歉是我们对话工具箱中最强大的工具之一。

sentences.en: They are so remarkably powerful.
sentences.zh: 它们非常强大。

sentences.en: And they're quick, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它们很快，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they, it doesn't take that many turns of a conversation to deliver an apology.
sentences.zh: 不需要太多的对话轮次就能表达歉意。

sentences.en: And they're just, they can do so much good.
sentences.zh: 它们可以带来很多好处。

sentences.en: And even though they're so powerful, many people are reluctant to give them.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们如此强大，但许多人还是不愿道歉。

sentences.en: Talk a little bit about that.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is, Alison?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么会这样，艾莉森？

sentences.en: Given how powerful they are, why are we so reluctant to deploy them?
sentences.zh: 考虑到它们如此强大，为什么我们如此不愿使用它们？

sentences.en: Apologizing requires that you make yourself vulnerable to the other person.
sentences.zh: 道歉要求你向对方展示自己的脆弱。

sentences.en: It feels like it requires you to humble yourself.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是要求你放下身段。

sentences.en: It can feel like you are admitting that you were wrong in some way.
sentences.zh: 这可能感觉像是你在承认自己在某种程度上错了。

sentences.en: And it makes yourself vulnerable to the other person because they could exploit that and say, oh, yes, you were wrong.
sentences.zh: 这会让你在对方面前显得脆弱，因为他们可能会利用这一点说：哦，没错，是你错了。

sentences.en: I was right.
sentences.zh: 我是对的。

sentences.en: And that just takes an incredible amount of humility.
sentences.zh: 而这需要极大的谦逊。

sentences.en: But in practice, when you go through with it and you apologize, it doesn't necessarily equate to an admission of blameworthiness.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，当你真正去做了并道歉时，这并不一定等同于承认自己有过错。

sentences.en: It just feels so good for the other person to be on the receiving end of it that it makes the conversation and the relationship so much better.
sentences.zh: 对方收到道歉的感觉非常好，这会让谈话和人际关系变得好得多。

sentences.en: I want you to tell me the story of when your son, Kevin, was a toddler.
sentences.zh: 我想请你讲讲你儿子凯文小时候的故事。

sentences.en: I understand to the extent that he could talk, you had a series of very difficult conversations.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，在他还只能说简单话语的时候，你们进行过一系列非常艰难的对话。

sentences.en: Tell me how those went and what happened, Alison.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，告诉我那些对话是怎么进行的，发生了什么。

sentences.en: Oh, my sweet Kevin.
sentences.zh: 哦，我可爱的凯文。

sentences.en: So Kevin's nine now.
sentences.zh: 凯文现在九岁了。

sentences.en: But back when he was, and he's a terrific kid, back when he was a toddler, he was a late talker.
sentences.zh: 但在他小时候——他是个很棒的孩子——他说话比较晚。

sentences.en: He was really frustrated and he had so many big ideas and he couldn't express them.
sentences.zh: 他当时非常沮丧，脑子里有很多想法却表达不出来。

sentences.en: And so he would get really angry and mad and yell and scream and sort of flop around.
sentences.zh: 所以他会变得非常愤怒、狂躁，大喊大叫，还会乱扑腾。

sentences.en: And one day during one of these sort of tantrums, he reared his head back and he and he sort of butted his head right into my face and he and he broke my nose.
sentences.zh: 有一天，在他又一次发脾气时，他猛地向后仰头，直接撞到了我的脸上，把我的鼻子撞断了。

sentences.en: And it was so painful and so physically painful, of course, but also emotionally painful.
sentences.zh: 那真的很痛，身体上的疼痛当然不用说，但心理上也同样痛苦。

sentences.en: Like as a mother, how do I have this child who's capable of like hurting me in this way?
sentences.zh: 作为一个母亲，我怎么会有这样一个能这样伤害我的孩子呢？

sentences.en: And how do I teach him to not be this way?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么教他不要这样呢？

sentences.en: And I just remember I plopped him down and I ran over to the mirror to see if my face was OK.
sentences.zh: 我只记得我把他放下，然后跑向镜子看看我的脸有没有事。

sentences.en: And it was a really dramatic moment that it was really hard.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常戏剧性的时刻，真的很难熬。

sentences.en: And he was so young, it was hard to decide how to react in that moment.
sentences.zh: 他当时太小了，很难决定在那一刻该如何反应。

sentences.en: I understand that you came back to this incident some years later, Alison.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，据我了解，几年后你又提起了这件事。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It became infamous in our family, the nose breaking incident with toddler Kevin.
sentences.zh: 那件事在我们家变得很有名，就是凯文小时候撞断我鼻子的那次事故。

sentences.en: And so over time, he heard me and my husband talk about this moment.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他听我和我丈夫谈起过这个时刻。

sentences.en: We told it to him as a story and, you know, he learned to talk.
sentences.zh: 我们把它当作一个故事讲给他听，你知道，他学会了说话。

sentences.en: He learned to regulate his emotions.
sentences.zh: 他学会了调节自己的情绪。

sentences.en: And he he sort of came to came to find this story like intriguing, like he couldn't believe that he would have behaved that way.
sentences.zh: 他开始觉得这个故事很有趣，他简直不敢相信自己曾经那样做过。

sentences.en: And one night he was probably seven or eight years old and we were reading together and he was reading one of his favorite books at the time, you know, Diary of a Wimpy Kid.
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上，他大概七八岁的时候，我们在一起读书，他当时正在读他最喜欢的书之一，你知道的，《小屁孩日记》。

sentences.en: A lot of kids love this series.
sentences.zh: 很多孩子都喜欢这个系列。

sentences.en: And the main character in the story typically can be sort of thoughtless and can be kind of cruel to his best friend.
sentences.zh: 书中的主角通常会被认为有些欠考虑，对最好的朋友也可能有点刻薄。

sentences.en: But there was a part of the book where Greg apologized to his best friend.
sentences.zh: 但书里有一段是格雷格向他最好的朋友道歉。

sentences.en: And it's a rare moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个罕见的时刻。

sentences.en: It was a very sort of kind moment for the character in the book.
sentences.zh: 对书中的角色来说，那是一个非常友善的时刻。

sentences.en: And in that moment, Kevin stopped reading and he looked up at me and he said, Mom, he said, yeah.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，凯文停止了阅读，他抬头看着我说：妈妈，他说，嗯。

sentences.en: And he said, do you remember when I broke your nose when I was a toddler?
sentences.zh: 然后他说：你还记得我小时候撞断你鼻子的事吗？

sentences.en: And I said, oh, yes, I do remember, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 我说：哦，是的，我记得，凯文。

sentences.en: I don't think I'll ever forget.
sentences.zh: 我想我永远不会忘记。

sentences.en: And he looked at me right in the eyes and he said, Mommy, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 他直视着我的眼睛说：妈妈，我真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: So sorry that I did that to you.
sentences.zh: 真的很抱歉我那样对你。

sentences.en: And my heart just sort of burst in the way that I had cried so much when he first had broken my nose.
sentences.zh: 我的心在那一刻融化了，就像他刚撞断我鼻子时我哭得那么伤心一样。

sentences.en: Now I was I was crying again, but this time out of pride.
sentences.zh: 现在我又哭了，但这次是因为自豪。

sentences.en: It was such a meaningful moment to see how he had grown from being this toddler struggling so much with language and his emotions.
sentences.zh: 看到他从那个在语言和情绪上挣扎的小孩成长到这一步，这是一个非常有意义的时刻。

sentences.en: And in such a short time, maybe five years later, I was in this place where he was able to own that and apologize and empathize and recognize my pain was just incredible.
sentences.zh: 在这么短的时间里，大概五年后，他能够承认错误、道歉、产生共情并意识到我的痛苦，这真是太不可思议了。
